cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your poem has my approval. The magazine rejected it because it deserves a whole booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I print that? The letter says 'weak imagery.' If it's just bad, I'd rather stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Publication is authorized. He means the images need more room; you needn't repeat his cramped layout.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you put that on the cover with your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My name is approved. Print it beneath 'A voice that deserves more space.' I'll stand where they can see me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 authorizes publication while distorting explicit criticism; A5 grants use of A name to protect B from abandoning writing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 weak-imagery wording contradicts the space cover; A3 visibly reframes it, and B4 signature demand causes A5 public ownership.

relationship.evidence: B2 threatens to stop and B4 asks A to stand behind reassurance, adding credible emotional and reputational pressure.

heightening.evidence: B4 name requirement makes the merciful story costly; A5 accepts exposure while retaining the authorizing manner.

specificity.evidence: A1 rejection, B2 quoted criticism and A5 cover line establish the actual submission outcome and proposed protection.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 prominent name beside the space claim is earned by B4 endorsement request, though the closing visibility phrase is figurative.
